sentences.en: Programming Throwdown, Episode 15, Lua.
sentences.zh: 《编程大乱斗》，第 15 期，Lua 语言。

sentences.en: Take it away, Jason.
sentences.zh: Jason，交给你了。

sentences.en: Hey, everybody.
sentences.zh: 嘿，大家好。

sentences.en: So, yeah, if you're wondering why the cadence of the show slowed down a little bit, it's been a little bit more than two weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，如果你在纳闷为什么节目的更新节奏慢了一点，因为已经过去两周多了。

sentences.en: People don't wonder anymore.
sentences.zh: 大家已经不纳闷了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's because Patrick and I were on vacation.
sentences.zh: 那是因为 Patrick 和我去度假了。

sentences.en: Patrick was in sunny, beautiful Florida.
sentences.zh: Patrick 去了阳光明媚、风景优美的佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: No, it was just really hot.
sentences.zh: 不，那里只是真的很热。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Already?
sentences.zh: 这么快就开始了？

sentences.en: It's only May.
sentences.zh: 现在才五月。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it was, like, really humid in 90-something.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但当时湿度很大，气温有九十多华氏度。

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And you don't realize how quickly – and we're going to sound really obnoxious, Jason, just forewarning people, because we're like, oh, sunny California.
sentences.zh: 你根本意识不到那种速度——Jason，我们接下来说的话可能会让人觉得很讨厌，先给你提个醒，因为我们当时就在说，哦，阳光明媚的加州。

sentences.en: But you really do get used to it really faSt.
sentences.zh: 但你确实会很快习惯那种天气。

sentences.en: And Florida has amazing weather.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达的天气其实很棒。

sentences.en: But I went back, and I sweated the whole time.
sentences.zh: 但我回去的时候，全程都在流汗。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember when I went back to Florida to visit my fam,
sentences.zh: 是啊，我记得我回佛罗里达探亲的时候，

sentences.en: I remember my glasses fogging up, like, when I got off the airplane, and, like, I couldn't see anything.
sentences.zh: 我记得我刚下飞机，眼镜就起雾了，什么都看不见。

sentences.en: And it was, like, just so damp.
sentences.zh: 而且感觉特别潮湿。

sentences.en: Yes, it's so much more humid and hot.
sentences.zh: 没错，那里确实比这儿潮湿闷热得多。

sentences.en: Ugh.
sentences.zh: 呃。

sentences.en: Yeah, terrible.
sentences.zh: 是啊，太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Now we sound like whiny, but that's okay.
sentences.zh: 现在我们听起来像是在发牢骚，不过没关系。

sentences.en: I was in not humid Alaska for a couple weeks, and that was pretty wild.
sentences.zh: 我在不潮湿的阿拉斯加待了几周，那段经历相当狂野。

sentences.en: We hiked all the way up to a glacier.
sentences.zh: 我们一路徒步爬上了一座冰川。

sentences.en: A couple of guys got buried in the snow, and we had snow shovels.
sentences.zh: 有几个人被埋在雪里了，我们带着雪铲。

sentences.en: We had to dig them out.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不把他们挖出来。

sentences.en: We were walking on these, like, snowshoes, which are, for people who don't know, they look kind of like a beaver's tail.
sentences.zh: 我们当时穿着雪鞋走路，对于不知道的人来说，那东西看起来有点像海狸的尾巴。

sentences.en: They're, like, really, like, flat and wide.
sentences.zh: 它们非常平坦且宽大。

sentences.en: And the idea is, like, you won't break through.
sentences.zh: 设计的初衷就是让你不会陷进去。

sentences.en: Because, you know, the way it works is the snow keeps piling on top, but the sun, especially during the day, sort of, like, heats up the snow,
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，它的原理是雪会不断堆积在上面，但太阳，尤其是在白天，会加热积雪，

sentences.en: and it creates kind of like a shell because it's, like, this water is heating and then cooling a lot.
sentences.zh: 这会形成一层外壳，因为水分在不断地加热和冷却。

sentences.en: And so you have this shell that's harder than the snow itself.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有这样一层比雪本身更硬的外壳。

sentences.en: And underneath the shell you have this soft snow.
sentences.zh: 而在外壳下面是松软的雪。

sentences.en: And so the snowshoes allow you to sort of walk on this shell without having to, like, trudge through to the snow, right?
sentences.zh: 所以雪鞋让你可以在这层外壳上行走，而不必在雪地里艰难跋涉，对吧？

sentences.en: But if you do fall in, your snowshoes, like, break through.
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的摔倒了，你的雪鞋就会把外壳踩破。

sentences.en: Then, like, you sink in, like, and people are sinking in, like, three, four feet into the snow.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会陷进去，就像其他人一样，陷进三四英尺深的雪里。

sentences.en: And then the snow sort of, like, it's not like quicksand.
sentences.zh: 而且雪的质地，它不像流沙。

sentences.en: Like, you don't sink in it or anything.
sentences.zh: 你不会沉下去什么的。

sentences.en: But, like, you fall through the snow, and then the snow, like, comes around you, kind of, and, like, entraps you.
sentences.zh: 但当你掉进雪里，雪会围住你，把你困住。

sentences.en: And especially since you have the snowshoes that are, like, attached to your feet, like, you can't lift them up because there's just too much snow has, like, collapsed on you.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为你的脚上还绑着雪鞋，你根本抬不起脚，因为有太多的雪塌在你身上了。

sentences.en: So somebody has to.
sentences.zh: 所以必须得有人帮忙。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We did all this to go to a glacier and take a lot of pictures.
sentences.zh: 我们做这一切就是为了去冰川拍很多照片。

sentences.en: But, you know, the adventure was the fun of it.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，冒险本身才是乐趣所在。

sentences.en: I think they have helicopters for that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们有直升机可以去那里。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: We could have taken a helicopter.
sentences.zh: 我们本可以坐直升机的。

sentences.en: Instead, we hiked it.
sentences.zh: 但我们选择了徒步。

sentences.en: So our parents, my in-laws came, and they actually took the helicopter.
sentences.zh: 我们的父母，也就是我的岳父母也来了，他们确实坐了直升机。

sentences.en: So we met them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在那里和他们会合了。

sentences.en: Did they meet you out there?
sentences.zh: 他们是在那儿和你碰头的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: We met them there, and then they took the helicopter back.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里会合，然后他们坐直升机回去了。

sentences.en: And it was about, I think it was, like, 8 to 10 miles.
sentences.zh: 全程大概有 8 到 10 英里吧。

sentences.en: So it was quite a hike.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一次相当长的徒步。

sentences.en: And we were pretty exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我们当时精疲力竭。

sentences.en: And, you know, at one point, the tour group leader was like, you know, you've only done 50% because we've got to go back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一次，旅游团领队说，你们才走了 50%，因为我们还得原路返回。

sentences.en: So those are the words you don't want to hear.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是你最不想听到的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, but some cool things about it.
sentences.zh: 不过，那里也有一些很酷的事情。

sentences.en: One, we saw some black bears.
sentences.zh: 第一，我们看到了一些黑熊。

sentences.en: That was pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 那真的很酷。

sentences.en: We learned the difference between black bear, grizzly bear, and polar bear.
sentences.zh: 我们了解了黑熊、灰熊和北极熊的区别。

sentences.en: So black bears are the least threatening.
sentences.zh: 黑熊的威胁性最小。

sentences.en: And they pretty much run away as soon as they see you.
sentences.zh: 它们一看到你基本上就会跑掉。

sentences.en: Grizzly bears and polar bears are, like, much more dangerous.
sentences.zh: 灰熊和北极熊要危险得多。

sentences.en: And brown bears are also pretty dangerous.
sentences.zh: 棕熊也相当危险。

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有别的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, the tour guides made this awesome stuff.
sentences.zh: 哦，导游做了很棒的东西。

sentences.en: They took, like, cocoa powder, like you used to make hot chocolate, and tang, and put it together.
sentences.zh: 他们拿了可可粉，就是平时冲热巧克力的那种，还有 Tang 橙味冲剂，混在一起。

sentences.en: And they made hot chocolate tang.
sentences.zh: 他们做出了热巧克力 Tang 饮料。

sentences.en: And it tasted like, you know those orange chocolates?
sentences.zh: 尝起来就像，你知道那种橙味巧克力吗？

sentences.en: It's like a huge orange-shaped chocolate.
sentences.zh: 就是那种巨大的橙子形状的巧克力。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，知道。

sentences.en: And you, like, slam it on the ground, and it breaks into pieces, you know?
sentences.zh: 你把它往地上一摔，它就会碎成几块，你知道吧？

sentences.en: It tasted like that.
sentences.zh: 尝起来就是那个味道。

sentences.en: It was really good.
sentences.zh: 非常好喝。

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I was kind of hiking in the wilderness.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我算是去荒野徒步了一趟。

sentences.en: But we're back with Lua.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在回归 Lua 了。

sentences.en: We survived.
sentences.zh: 我们活下来了。

sentences.en: Yes, we did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们做到了。

sentences.en: It was pretty awesome.
sentences.zh: 那真的很棒。

sentences.en: I have some pictures posted.
sentences.zh: 我发布了一些照片。

sentences.en: I'll share them with the Mamehub page so that anyone who's following the page will get to see the pictures of the hike.
sentences.zh: 我会把它们分享到 Mamehub 页面上，这样关注该页面的任何人都能看到徒步的照片。

sentences.en: Or their programming throwdown page, maybe, too.
sentences.zh: 或者可能也会发到《编程大乱斗》的页面上。

sentences.en: That's right, the programming throwdown page.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是《编程大乱斗》的页面。

sentences.en: What did I say?
sentences.zh: 我刚才说了什么？

sentences.en: You said Mamehub.
sentences.zh: 你说的是 Mamehub。

sentences.en: You have too many pages.
sentences.zh: 你的页面太多了。

sentences.en: Oh, I know.
sentences.zh: 哦，我知道。

sentences.en: I have too many, for real.
sentences.zh: 说真的，我页面太多了。

sentences.en: Well, I think I'm going to add a third page now, so it's going to be just ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我现在要再加第三个页面了，那简直太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 啊哦。

sentences.en: Spoiler alert.
sentences.zh: 剧透预警。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, the news of the week is Facebook.
sentences.zh: 那么，本周的新闻是关于 Facebook 的。

sentences.en: So, Jason, I think, uses Facebook some.
sentences.zh: 我想 Jason 平时会用一些 Facebook。

sentences.en: I have an account, I think, somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我好像在什么地方有个账号。

sentences.en: All I know is Facebook keeps emailing me and saying, you have, like, 30-something friend requests.
sentences.zh: 我只知道 Facebook 不停地给我发邮件，说我有三十多个好友请求。

sentences.en: And I'm just like, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我对此完全不在意。

sentences.en: You should detect it.
sentences.zh: 你应该检测一下。

sentences.en: I haven't logged in in years.
sentences.zh: 我已经好几年没登录过了。

sentences.en: So, I got one when it first came out.
sentences.zh: 我是在它刚出来的时候注册了一个。

sentences.en: I use Facebook as, like, the OAuth.
sentences.zh: 我把 Facebook 当作 OAuth 使用。

sentences.en: You know, like, some things now will let you log in using your Facebook ID.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在有些东西允许你用 Facebook ID 登录。

sentences.en: Like, single sign-on.
sentences.zh: 就像单点登录一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I'll do that.
sentences.zh: 我会用那个功能。

sentences.en: But that's about all I use it for.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外我就不用它了。

sentences.en: So, actually, I'm interested how many of Facebook's 900 million users are doing that.
sentences.zh: 其实我很好奇 Facebook 的 9 亿用户中有多少人在这样做。

sentences.en: Like, only interaction.
sentences.zh: 就只是这种互动。

sentences.en: Or is it 900 million is, like, registered?
sentences.zh: 还是说 9 亿只是注册用户数？

sentences.en: And then I forget how many they claim are active.
sentences.zh: 我忘了他们声称的活跃用户是多少了。

sentences.en: But how many of their active users, you know, are logging on to Facebook.com, being served ads, you know, and, you know, interfacing with the content.
sentences.zh: 但他们的活跃用户里，有多少人是在登录 Facebook.com，浏览广告，以及与内容进行交互的呢？

sentences.en: How many are accessing it, like, on a mobile device where you don't get ads.
sentences.zh: 有多少人是在移动设备上访问的，而那里是没有广告的。

sentences.en: And then how many are just using it, like, you, for, you know, just logging into other websites, authenticating with stuff, or just playing games.
sentences.zh: 还有多少人像你一样，只是用它来登录其他网站、进行身份验证，或者只是玩游戏。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I read an article that over a third of people just log on Facebook to play Zynga games.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我读过一篇文章，说超过三分之一的人登录 Facebook 只是为了玩 Zynga 游戏。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，就是这样。

sentences.en: Farmville.
sentences.zh: 《农场小镇》。

sentences.en: Nobody admits to playing that game.
sentences.zh: 没人承认自己在玩那个游戏。

sentences.en: But I know there has to be a ton of people playing that game.
sentences.zh: 但我知道肯定有很多人在玩。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，绝对有。

sentences.en: There's got to be.
sentences.zh: 肯定有。

sentences.en: But, you know, I mean, even just, even if it's true, and people aren't, you know, the whole wall, post on the wall, share with your friends, if that's kind of, like,
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，即使这是真的，人们不再在墙上发帖、不再与朋友分享，如果这些功能已经，

sentences.en: gone with the dodo, it's still pretty useful technology.
sentences.zh: 像渡渡鸟一样灭绝了，它仍然是一项非常有用的技术。

sentences.en: You know, just being able to identify people and their relationships.
sentences.zh: 你知道，仅仅是能够识别用户及其社交关系这一点。

sentences.en: And a lot of applications need something like that to be, you know, even better.
sentences.zh: 很多应用都需要这样的功能才能变得更好。

sentences.en: But is it worth hundreds of billions of dollars?
sentences.zh: 但它真的值数千亿美元吗？

sentences.en: And that's the question that was asked at the end of last week.
sentences.zh: 这就是上周末提出的问题。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Facebook IPO'd their initial public offering.
sentences.zh: 所以，Facebook 进行了首次公开募股（IPO）。

sentences.en: And Jason and I are not business majors.
sentences.zh: Jason 和我都不是商科专业的。

sentences.en: We are not financial students.
sentences.zh: 我们也不是金融专业的学生。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Let's put a disclaimer here.
sentences.zh: 我们先声明一下。

sentences.en: You know, we don't take this as stock market advice or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，别把这当作股票市场建议或类似的东西。

sentences.en: This should not be construed as trading advice in any shape or form.
sentences.zh: 这不应被解读为任何形式的交易建议。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so it was really weird.
sentences.zh: 但，确实，这真的很奇怪。

sentences.en: We were watching it, you know, being in the tech industry.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在关注它，毕竟身处科技行业。

sentences.en: People at work were interested in this because it's a very, it hit mainstream, right?
sentences.zh: 同事们对此很感兴趣，因为它非常主流，对吧？

sentences.en: So, even the morning news was covering Facebook's IPO and it being local to this area, the Silicon Valley, that, you know, it was big news.
sentences.zh: 所以，连早间新闻都在报道 Facebook 的 IPO，而且它就在我们这个地区——硅谷，所以这确实是大新闻。

sentences.en: And so, people were watching it.
sentences.zh: 因此，大家都在关注它。

sentences.en: And it was just one of the weirdest things, you know, I've seen that people were just talking about it.
sentences.zh: 那真是最奇怪的事情之一，你知道，我看到人们都在谈论这件事。

sentences.en: And then stuff just seemed to go terribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 然后事情似乎就变得一团糟了。

sentences.en: So, when it first opened, it turns out afterwards, I was trying to read because, you know, when I, I think it was LinkedIn or Groupon had IPO'd.
sentences.zh: 所以，当它刚上市时，事后我才了解到，我当时试着去读相关报道，因为你知道，我想当时是 LinkedIn 或 Groupon 进行了首次公开募股（IPO）。

sentences.en: I had tried to watch it like because I was curious what would happen.
sentences.zh: 我当时试着去关注，因为我很好奇会发生什么。

sentences.en: And it didn't open with the market.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有随市场开盘。

sentences.en: But this was expected.
sentences.zh: 但这其实是在预料之中的。

sentences.en: And actually, news reports said this was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 事实上，新闻报道也说这会发生。

sentences.en: But Facebook was supposed to start trading when the NASDAQ opened.
sentences.zh: 但 Facebook 本应在纳斯达克开盘时就开始交易。

sentences.en: They're going to trade on the NASDAQ or they are trading on the NASDAQ.
sentences.zh: 他们要在纳斯达克交易，或者说他们正在纳斯达克交易。

sentences.en: But it turned out the NASDAQ had technical difficulties that delayed the start of trading for like almost three hours or two hours, two and a half hours, something like that.
sentences.zh: 但结果纳斯达克出现了技术故障，导致交易推迟了大约三个小时，或者说两个小时，两个半小时，差不多是这样。

sentences.en: And so, I read a little bit about it trying to understand.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了一些相关内容，试图去理解。

sentences.en: And the best explanation I could kind of come across was that they, the IPO price, that very first price that it's going to start at is calculated by how many people kind of say,
sentences.zh: 我能找到的最好解释是，IPO 价格，也就是它开始交易的第一个价格，是根据有多少人表示：

sentences.en: I'm going to buy shares at whatever price it opens at, right?
sentences.zh: “无论开盘价是多少，我都要买入”，对吧？

sentences.en: So, before the market opens, they put in an order with their broker.
sentences.zh: 所以，在市场开盘前，他们会向经纪人下达指令。

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: “我不在乎价格。”

sentences.en: Buy it right away, you know?
sentences.zh: “直接买入”，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And those are matched, which is the whole purpose of, you know, the exchanges.
sentences.zh: 这些指令会被撮合，这正是交易所存在的全部意义。

sentences.en: So, the New York Stock Exchange, NASDAQ, the Chicago Board of Exchange, these different markets,

sentences.zh: 我必须序列化所有数据，把数据——可能是一堆类、函数之类的东西——转换成类似 MySQL 表的格式。

sentences.en: I have to create the schema.
sentences.zh: 我必须创建数据库架构。

sentences.en: Like, there's so much overhead, right?
sentences.zh: 你看，这中间有太多的额外开销了，对吧？

sentences.en: You can avoid some of that by using SQLite.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过使用 SQLite 来避免其中的一些问题。

sentences.en: But maybe that's for another week.
sentences.zh: 但也许那是下周的话题了。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Well, even with SQLite, you have to do a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，即使是用 SQLite，你也得做很多类似的工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, but you still have some of those problems, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，但你仍然会遇到其中一些问题，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, you have to create the tables.
sentences.zh: 是的，你还是得创建表。

sentences.en: Sorry, not to rain on your parade.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我不是想泼你冷水。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the simplest thing, the simplest database that, well, I can think of, at least, is a key value pair, right?
sentences.zh: 所以最简单的东西，至少我能想到的最简单的数据库，就是键值对，对吧？

sentences.en: So basically, you just have a list of keys and, like, a hash table, basically, but on disk.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你只需要一个键列表，就像哈希表一样，只不过是存在磁盘上的。

sentences.en: And so that's exactly what BerkeleyDB is.
sentences.zh: 而这正是 BerkeleyDB 的本质。

sentences.en: It's just a simple hash table that persists the disk.
sentences.zh: 它就是一个简单的、持久化到磁盘的哈希表。

sentences.en: And you can put in keys.
sentences.zh: 你可以存入键。

sentences.en: You can put in key value pairs, and then later on, you can search for the key, and you can get the value.
sentences.zh: 你可以存入键值对，稍后你就可以通过搜索键来获取对应的值。

sentences.en: And it does some clever caching.
sentences.zh: 它还做了一些巧妙的缓存处理。

sentences.en: But if you fall through the cache, you know, it has a backup on disk.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没命中缓存，你知道的，它在磁盘上还有备份。

sentences.en: And it's also transactional.
sentences.zh: 而且它还支持事务。

sentences.en: What that means is you can queue up a bunch of commands, and then you can commit the commands.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以排队执行一堆命令，然后一次性提交这些命令。

sentences.en: And so let's say, for example, let's say I load Patrick's profile.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，假设我加载了 Patrick 的个人资料。

sentences.en: I'm a web server, and Patrick logs into my server on his computer.
sentences.zh: 我是一个 Web 服务器，Patrick 在他的电脑上登录了我的服务器。

sentences.en: And he goes and, like, changes his password.
sentences.zh: 然后他去修改了他的密码。

sentences.en: But then at exactly the same time, evil Patrick, who's masquerading as regular Patrick, is on Patrick's phone and changes his password right there on the phone, too.
sentences.zh: 但就在同一时间，冒充 Patrick 的“邪恶 Patrick”正在用 Patrick 的手机，直接在手机上也修改了他的密码。

sentences.en: Or changes something else.
sentences.zh: 或者修改了其他东西。

sentences.en: Changes his, like, profile picture to a Hello Kitty picture.
sentences.zh: 比如把他的头像改成了 Hello Kitty 的图片。

sentences.en: Or, like, at exactly the same time, you know, that can cause issues.
sentences.zh: 或者，就在同一时间，你知道的，这可能会引发问题。

sentences.en: Like, you could end up, like, saving two things twice, and one can collide and things like that.
sentences.zh: 比如，你最终可能会保存两次东西，导致冲突之类的。

sentences.en: So you need to support transactions to deal with things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要支持事务来处理这类情况。

sentences.en: So the thing that comes in second, the transactional fail, it'll say, hey, something weird has happened.
sentences.zh: 所以后进来的那个事务会失败，它会提示说，嘿，发生了一些奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: This data has been modified.
sentences.zh: 数据已经被修改了。

sentences.en: You need to take a look at this and sort this out.
sentences.zh: 你需要检查一下并解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So it handles, like, the very basics of what you need to have what's called an ACID-compliant database.
sentences.zh: 所以它处理了所谓的 ACID 兼容数据库所需的最基本功能。

sentences.en: And ACID, I don't remember, do you know what it stands for, Patrick?
sentences.zh: 至于 ACID，我不记得了，你知道它代表什么吗，Patrick？

sentences.en: It's, like, atomic...
sentences.zh: 它是，原子性……

sentences.en: Consistency?
sentences.zh: 一致性？

sentences.en: Isolation?
sentences.zh: 隔离性？

sentences.en: Durability?
sentences.zh: 持久性？

sentences.en: Ah, there you go.
sentences.zh: 啊，对了，就是这些。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 完美。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错。

sentences.en: So you want that.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要这些。

sentences.en: So BerkeleyDB has a bunch of bindings, like C, C++.
sentences.zh: BerkeleyDB 有很多语言绑定，比如 C、C++。

sentences.en: You know, I think there's a Python binding.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想应该有 Python 绑定。

sentences.en: Actually, I think it's part of Python, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实，我觉得它本身就是 Python 的一部分。

sentences.en: Now, so if you're using Java, now, Java already has a really nice collections framework, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你用的是 Java，Java 本身已经有一套非常棒的集合框架了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, Java has map and, you know, hash map, tree map, linked list, array list, all these cool things.
sentences.zh: 比如 Java 有 Map，还有 HashMap、TreeMap、LinkedList、ArrayList，所有这些很酷的东西。

sentences.en: And since Java already has all this infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 既然 Java 已经有了这些基础设施。

sentences.en: There's something called JDBM, which basically what it does is it gives you a map, like a Java map, but that map is backed by, back to disk.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫 JDBM 的东西，它基本上就是为你提供一个 Map，一个 Java Map，但这个 Map 是由磁盘支持的。

sentences.en: So, in other words, like, you can write your program and have everything in memory, like all your usernames and passwords and all that in memory.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你可以编写程序，把所有东西都放在内存里，比如所有的用户名、密码等等，都在内存里。

sentences.en: And then once your program gets more mature and you say, okay, I want to deploy this.
sentences.zh: 然后当你的程序变得更成熟，你想部署它的时候。

sentences.en: You can just replace the new hash map with JDBM3 hash map.
sentences.zh: 你只需要把新的 HashMap 替换成 JDBM3 的 HashMap。

sentences.en: And it'll just deal with everything under the hood.
sentences.zh: 它就会在底层处理好一切。

sentences.en: So, it'll put things to disk when you need to go to disk.
sentences.zh: 所以，当需要存盘时，它会自动存到磁盘上。

sentences.en: It'll load things from disk, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 它会自动从磁盘加载数据，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And actually, BerkeleyDB is the most popular database because it's installed, like, multiple times on everyone's machine.
sentences.zh: 事实上，BerkeleyDB 是最流行的数据库，因为它在每个人的机器上都被安装了好多次。

sentences.en: Like, even if you run Windows, Windows actually uses BerkeleyDB for a number of things.
sentences.zh: 比如，即使你运行的是 Windows，Windows 实际上也在很多地方使用了 BerkeleyDB。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So, this doesn't handle over the network, though, right?
sentences.zh: 不过，它不支持网络访问，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, this is just for, like, local persistence to disk.
sentences.zh: 这只是用于本地磁盘持久化，对吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And the other thing is it doesn't handle multi-processor.
sentences.zh: 另外，它也不支持多进程。

sentences.en: Although now there are some versions that are starting to get into that.
sentences.zh: 虽然现在有一些版本开始涉足这方面了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But for the most part, it's, you know, if you have a single program, it could be multi-threaded.
sentences.zh: 但大部分情况下，如果你只有一个程序，它可以是多线程的。

sentences.en: And I think we talked about this.
sentences.zh: 我想我们之前讨论过这个。

sentences.en: But just to recap really quick, multi-threaded means you have, you know, a bunch of different threads that could all be doing different things,
sentences.zh: 但简单回顾一下，多线程意味着你有许多不同的线程，它们可能都在做不同的事情，

sentences.en: but they're all sharing the same memory.
sentences.zh: 但它们共享同一块内存。

sentences.en: Versus multi-process, each one is a completely different program.
sentences.zh: 而多进程则是每个进程都是一个完全独立的程序。

sentences.en: And so, BerkeleyDB and JDBM don't support multi-process yet, but they support multi-threaded.
sentences.zh: 所以，BerkeleyDB 和 JDBM 目前还不支持多进程，但它们支持多线程。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, I mean, unless you're, you know, a lot of websites use MySQL.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，除非你是……你知道，很多网站都用 MySQL。

sentences.en: But really, unless you're, like, some kind of powerhouse, you'd be totally fine.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，除非你是什么大型机构，否则用这个完全没问题。

sentences.en: Like, if you're doing your own coding, you'd be totally fine using something like this.
sentences.zh: 如果你是自己写代码，用这种东西完全足够了。

sentences.en: And you'd save yourself a ton of time.
sentences.zh: 而且能为你节省大量时间。

sentences.en: And then I think if you use, like, a key value pattern like that, right, so if you can reduce it to something simple like that,
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果你使用像那样的键值模式，如果你能把它简化成那样，

sentences.en: then I think it would be easy to move it over to network.
sentences.zh: 那么我觉得迁移到网络上也会很容易。

sentences.en: Like, I think Redis and other databases are kind of the same idea, but for network-connected things.
sentences.zh: 比如，我觉得 Redis 和其他数据库也是类似的思路，只不过是针对网络连接的场景。

sentences.en: So if you wanted to add in sharing with other people, if you're using this key value mentality, there are other solutions that will take you to the next step.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想增加与他人共享的功能，如果你采用了这种键值思维，还有其他解决方案可以带你进入下一步。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's CouchDB, Redis.
sentences.zh: 有 CouchDB、Redis。

sentences.en: There's HBase.
sentences.zh: 还有 HBase。

sentences.en: There's a ton of them.
sentences.zh: 有很多这样的数据库。

sentences.en: I mean, we should maybe talk about, dedicate some time to that, you know, in the future, because those are actually really, really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们以后也许应该专门花点时间聊聊这个，因为它们确实非常、非常有趣。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: Audacity。

sentences.zh: 所以我决定我们得聊聊它，因为你们现在就是通过它来收听我们的节目的。

sentences.zh: 这就是你们现在收听我们节目的力量来源。

sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.zh: 你知道，以前要做这种事，你得买昂贵的软件。

sentences.zh: 然后，当 Audacity 出现时，它真的改变了一切。

sentences.en: So you can record, you can clean up, you can edit, you can mix multiple tracks together.
sentences.zh: 你可以录音、清理音频、剪辑、混合多条音轨。

sentences.zh: 如果我们有很酷的音效，我们也能加进去。

sentences.zh: 目前为止，我们用它来制作片头和片尾。

sentences.en: You know, all that kind of stuff we do using Audacity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有这些东西我们都是用 Audacity 做的。

sentences.zh: 它太棒了，而且是免费的。

sentences.zh: 还是开源的。

sentences.en: Or maybe that was after.

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, at some point I used these prograMs.

sentences.en: And it was just, like, they were very slow and clunky.
sentences.zh: 而且它们非常慢，用起来很笨重。

sentences.en: And, you know, Audacity works on Windows, Linux, Mac.
sentences.zh: 而 Audacity 支持 Windows、Linux 和 Mac。

sentences.zh: 它在任何系统上都能用。

sentences.en: Really nice interface.

sentences.en: Let's you do all the, like, they added all the polish, you know.

sentences.en: Like, it won't use your microphone that's hooked up to your computer if you have the headphones plugged in and things like that.

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's very nice.
sentences.zh: 它非常好用。

sentences.en: Very powerful.
sentences.zh: 功能非常强大。

sentences.en: And if you don't know about it and you want to do any sort of audio editing, that's where you should go.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不知道它，但又想做任何音频剪辑，你应该去试试这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是啊，完全同意。

sentences.zh: 那么。

sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊 Lua。

sentences.en: Lua.
sentences.zh: Lua。

sentences.en: Now, how similar is Lua to a luau?
sentences.zh: 那么，Lua 和夏威夷宴会（luau）有多像？

sentences.en: Very similar.
sentences.zh: 非常像。

sentences.en: Because I like luau's.
sentences.zh: 因为我喜欢夏威夷宴会。

sentences.en: I love luau's.
sentences.zh: 我爱死夏威夷宴会了。

sentences.en: The only thing, sometimes, like, you see that pig.
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，有时候你会看到那只猪。

sentences.en: What is that called when they have the pig with the apple in its mouth?
sentences.zh: 嘴里叼着苹果的那种猪叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, suckling.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，乳猪。

sentences.en: Suckling pig.
sentences.zh: 烤乳猪。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, the suckling pig.
sentences.zh: 是啊，烤乳猪。

sentences.en: Like, I think Lua core dumps a lot more than the suckling pig.
sentences.zh: 我觉得 Lua 出现核心转储（core dump）的频率比烤乳猪高多了。

sentences.en: But that might be because the pig is dead.
sentences.zh: 但这可能是因为猪已经死了。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Okay, we might have lost people from our trying to be punny.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们可能因为试图讲冷笑话而失去了一些听众。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so Lua originated in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 但总之，Lua 起源于巴西。

sentences.en: It actually has an interesting history.
sentences.zh: 它其实有一段很有趣的历史。

sentences.en: At some point, Brazil actually had, like, some kind of law where they weren't allowed.
sentences.zh: 在某个时期，巴西甚至出台过某种法律，禁止使用它们。

sentences.en: You weren't allowed to import source code.
sentences.zh: 你不被允许导入源代码。

sentences.en: It's, like, the craziest thing I've ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 这简直是我听过最疯狂的事情了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's, like, almost like a trade embargo of sorts.
sentences.zh: 没错，这几乎就像是一种贸易禁运。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Like, we want our country to stay behind in technology.
sentences.zh: 就好像是说，我们希望国家的技术水平保持落后。

sentences.en: Maybe that's why so many of them use Orchid.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是为什么他们那么多人使用 Orchid 的原因吧。

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so there's – so there's – so for people who don't know, Orchid is a social network sort of, like, predecessor to Facebook or any of these.
sentences.zh: 不过，对于不知道的人来说，Orchid 是一种社交网络，算是 Facebook 或类似平台的前身。

sentences.en: It was, like, even earlier than Friendster.
sentences.zh: 它甚至比 Friendster 还要早。

sentences.en: And for some reason, it's, like, massive adoption in Brazil, but that's it.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，它在巴西有着极高的普及率，但也仅限于此。

sentences.en: Although they said it's not anymore.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们说现在已经不是这样了。

sentences.en: Facebook surpassed Orchid popularity in Brazil.
sentences.zh: Facebook 在巴西的受欢迎程度已经超过了 Orchid。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's about time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也是时候了。

sentences.en: But, anyway, so, yeah, it started off in Brazil as a need to sort of create embeddable language.
sentences.zh: 总之，它在巴西起步时，是为了满足某种嵌入式语言的需求。

sentences.en: But, you know, actually, although it sort of sounds like something – you know, it was created because there was no alternatives in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 但其实，虽然听起来像是——你知道，它是为了解决巴西当时没有替代品的问题而创建的。

sentences.en: The reality is it's a fantastic embeddable language.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，它本身就是一种非常出色的嵌入式语言。

sentences.en: And, you know, at the time it was created, the only language even remotely, you know, similar in its ability to sort of integrate with other languages is TCL or Tickle,
sentences.zh: 而且在它诞生的时候，唯一在与其他语言集成能力上稍微有点类似的语言是 TCL，或者叫 Tickle，

sentences.en: as some people call it.
sentences.zh: 有些人是这么叫的。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you want, in Lua, you can say, you know, you can create a new table like my table equals, you know, open brace, close brace.

sentences.en: And my table Monday is one, Tuesday is two, Wednesday is three, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: Monday 是 1，Tuesday 是 2，Wednesday 是 3，以此类推。

sentences.en: And so then later on you could say, well, what is Wednesday?

sentences.en: But basically, you know, it's an associative array, so it just uses the equals operation for whatever type it's using.

sentences.en: So you could have a table with tables in it, or you could have a table that maps numbers to strings.

sentences.en: It doesn't matter, right?

sentences.en: So, I mean, this is the second time we've kind of brought this up, but maybe a quick explanation of hash tables.

sentences.en: Just like the idea of hashing is just taking one thing, running some sort of function on it, and producing a number.
sentences.zh: 哈希的概念就是取一个东西，对其运行某种函数，然后产生一个数字。

sentences.en: So, like, if you take one number, you might multiply it by 10, and that's your hashing function.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你取一个数字，把它乘以 10，这就是你的哈希函数。

sentences.en: That's not a very good hashing function.
sentences.zh: 那不是一个很好的哈希函数。

sentences.en: And then typically, like, the simplest way to think about a hash table is just an array.
sentences.zh: 通常来说，理解哈希表最简单的方法就是把它看作一个数组。

sentences.en: So let's say you have an array that's size 10, and you want to store things in it that aren't necessarily obvious, you know, that it should be an array.
sentences.zh: 假设你有一个大小为 10 的数组，你想在里面存储一些东西，而这些东西并不明显应该放在数组里。

sentences.en: So, like, to Jason's point, if you want to store the day of the week Sunday somewhere in there, where should Sunday go?
sentences.zh: 所以，按照 Jason 的观点，如果你想把星期天（Sunday）存进去，它应该放在哪儿？

sentences.en: Well, you could take the letters of Sunday and, like, add the ASCII value of each of the letters, you know, modulus.
sentences.zh: 你可以取 Sunday 的字母，把每个字母的 ASCII 值加起来，然后取模。

sentences.en: So divide that and take the remainder of 10 and say, like, that's the index in the array I'm going to use to store anything that's Sunday.
sentences.zh: 除以 10 取余数，然后说，这就是我要用来存储 Sunday 的数组索引。

sentences.en: Or, like Jason's saying, you can use it kind of, like, more like maybe an enumeration, where Sunday is kind of like the zero with object or store zero in it.

sentences.en: So when you look it up later in the table, you can pull out the number zero, and you know that that is the value Sunday should have.
sentences.zh: 这样当你以后在表中查找时，就能取出数字 0，你就知道这就是 Sunday 应该有的值。

sentences.en: And so there's something in hash tables called collisions.

sentences.zh: 哈希表的处理方式是，当它插入 Wednesday 时，会发现 Sunday 已经在表里了，但它们是两个不同的东西。

sentences.en: So then it'll do, like, what's called a deep compare.

sentences.en: So first it'll compare just the hashing, the hash function.
sentences.zh: 首先它会比较哈希函数的结果。

sentences.en: And if there's a collision, it'll do a deep compare and say, is this the same item?
sentences.zh: 如果发生冲突，它会进行深度比较，判断这是不是同一个项目。

sentences.en: Should I replace it?

sentences.en: If it's not, then it'll, there's many different things it can do then.

sentences.en: But yeah, basically, a hash table is a way to get really fast lookup and entry of iteMs.

sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，你知道，斐波那契数列的 1 是 1，2 是 1。

sentences.en: Two is one, but then three is going to be f of one plus f of two, which is two.
sentences.zh: 2 是 1，但 3 将会是 f(1) 加 f(2)，也就是 2。

sentences.en: And the Fibonacci sequence of four is going to be f of two plus f of three, which is three.
sentences.zh: 而斐波那契数列的 4 将会是 f(2) 加 f(3)，也就是 3。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they were able to use the meta tables to say, okay, I create a table, and one is one and two is one.
sentences.zh: 所以他们能够使用元表来说，好的，我创建一个表，1 是 1，2 是 1。

sentences.en: And then I create a meta table where if they want anything besides one or two, it's the table entry of n minus two plus the table of entry of n minus one.
sentences.zh: 然后我创建一个元表，如果他们想要 1 或 2 以外的任何值，它就是表项 n-2 加上表项 n-1。

sentences.en: And so that'll kind of recurse backwards, and Lua is smart about caching.
sentences.zh: 这样它就会向后递归，而且 Lua 在缓存方面很聪明。

sentences.en: So let's say something happens where all of a sudden you have an influx of Spanish-speaking people hitting your website, and everyone wants Domingo all of a sudden.
sentences.zh: 所以假设发生了一些情况，突然有一大批讲西班牙语的人访问你的网站，每个人突然都想要 Domingo。

sentences.en: But Lua will actually cache that value, so you won't have to just keep hitting the database.
sentences.zh: 但 Lua 实际上会缓存该值，所以你就不必一直去访问数据库了。

sentences.en: So it's clever about that.
sentences.zh: 所以它在这方面很聪明。

sentences.en: This is also called memoization when you do, like, well, memoization is more with respect to recursion.
sentences.zh: 这也被称为记忆化（memoization），当你做，嗯，记忆化更多是与递归相关的。

sentences.en: But if you do these kind of things where, like, you cache data in a table, in a hash table, so you don't have to keep calling a function, Lua will do that for you,
sentences.zh: 但如果你做这类事情，比如你在表、哈希表中缓存数据，这样你就不必一直调用函数，Lua 会为你做这些，

sentences.en: which is pretty clever.
sentences.zh: 这非常巧妙。

sentences.en: So it's cool because in some ways you're able to just use a table that, in theory, has infinitely many entries in it, has all of the Fibonacci sequence in it.
sentences.zh: 这很酷，因为在某种程度上，你能够只使用一个理论上拥有无限条目的表，拥有整个斐波那契数列。

sentences.en: But then only when you actually try to use some entry of the Fibonacci sequence does it actually go and figure out what that number should be.
sentences.zh: 但只有当你真正尝试使用斐波那契数列的某个条目时，它才会去计算出那个数字应该是多少。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is also called lazy, like either lazy loading or, in this case, lazy calculations.
sentences.zh: 这也被称为惰性，比如惰性加载，或者在这种情况下，惰性计算。

sentences.en: It only calculates what it needs to.
sentences.zh: 它只计算它需要的部分。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So what are some of the – so we kind of hinted at some of the strengths of Lua that we already mentioned that was used as, like, a scripting language.
sentences.zh: 那么，有哪些——我们已经暗示了 Lua 的一些优势，我们之前提到过它被用作脚本语言。

sentences.en: And it's kind of used as a scripting language, I guess, because it works so well with C and C++.
sentences.zh: 我想它被用作脚本语言，是因为它与 C 和 C++ 配合得非常好。

sentences.en: It's really easy to embed it.
sentences.zh: 嵌入它非常容易。

sentences.en: And you said you've worked with it this way before?
sentences.zh: 你说过你以前这样用过它？

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对用过。

sentences.en: So Lua was designed to integrate with C specifically, but later on with C++.
sentences.zh: 所以 Lua 被设计为专门与 C 集成，后来也支持 C++。

sentences.en: And so, you know, just to put this, like, in just a contrast, let's say you want to embed, like, Python, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，为了对比一下，假设你想嵌入 Python，例如。

sentences.en: Well, you have to use this, like, really clunky, like, Python C API, and, like, everything is kind of based on these functions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你必须使用这种非常笨重的 Python C API，而且一切都基于这些函数。

sentences.en: And you have to, like, convert, like, Python – oh, you know, I forgot the –
sentences.zh: 而且你必须，比如，转换 Python——哦，你知道，我忘了——

sentences.en: Well, so there's calling C from Python, and then there's scripting events in C with Python.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有从 Python 调用 C，也有用 Python 在 C 中编写脚本事件。

sentences.en: Right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And so both of those get complicated because you have to transmute the types.
sentences.zh: 所以这两者都变得很复杂，因为你必须转换类型。

sentences.en: So in Python, you have lists, you have dictionaries, you have all these different types, right, as we talked about at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 在 Python 中，你有列表、字典，你有所有这些不同的类型，对吧，正如我们在开头讨论的那样。

sentences.en: And each of those, you have to create some kind of analog on the C or C++ side.
sentences.zh: 对于每一种类型，你都必须在 C 或 C++ 端创建某种模拟。

sentences.en: Or you have to create some kind of, like, accessors.
sentences.zh: 或者你必须创建某种访问器。

sentences.en: So you have to be able to say, like, oh, this is a list in Python, so I want to get the fourth element in this list in my C++ program.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须能够说，哦，这是 Python 中的一个列表，所以我想在我的 C++ 程序中获取这个列表的第四个元素。

sentences.en: Or I have this C++ array, I want Python to think of this as a list, you know.
sentences.zh: 或者我有这个 C++ 数组，我想让 Python 把它看作一个列表，你知道。

sentences.en: And this kind of stuff ends up becoming, like, no matter how you do it, it ends up becoming really clunky.
sentences.zh: 这种事情最终变得，无论你怎么做，最终都会变得非常笨重。

sentences.en: Lua, you know, it's kind of a double-edged sword.
sentences.zh: Lua，你知道，它是一把双刃剑。

sentences.en: Like, it only has tables, but on the plus side, it only has tables, right, which map exactly to C++, you know, hash maps.
sentences.zh: 它只有表，但好的一面是，它只有表，对吧，这完全映射到 C++ 的哈希映射。

sentences.en: So it makes it very easy to integrate the two languages.
sentences.zh: 所以这使得集成这两种语言变得非常容易。

sentences.en: And even easier because people have, since so many people are doing this with Lua or embedding it, they've created some amazingly streamlined libraries to make this happen.
sentences.zh: 而且更容易，因为人们，由于很多人都在用 Lua 或嵌入它，他们已经创建了一些非常精简的库来实现这一点。

sentences.en: So one is LuaBind, which I used briefly.
sentences.zh: 一个是 LuaBind，我简要使用过。

sentences.en: But the second one I'm more familiar with is called Diluculum, which I think it's some African word or something.
sentences.zh: 但我更熟悉第二个，叫 Diluculum，我想那是一个非洲词汇之类的。

sentences.en: But we have a link to the, in the show notes, so you guys can look it up.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目说明里有链接，所以你们可以去查一下。

sentences.en: But, basically, it has a, it's for C++, and it has a thing that maps, like, Lua tables, actually anything in Lua, to the analog in C++.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，它适用于 C++，并且有一个东西可以将 Lua 表，实际上是 Lua 中的任何东西，映射到 C++ 中的模拟对象。

sentences.en: And it sort of does it all transparently.
sentences.zh: 它几乎是透明地完成这一切。

sentences.en: So you can just say, hey, you know, go to the Lua world and get me this variable.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以直接说，嘿，去 Lua 世界帮我获取这个变量。

sentences.en: And even, like, on the other side in your Lua program, you can say, hey, go to the C++ world and get me this variable.
sentences.zh: 甚至在另一端，在你的 Lua 程序中，你可以说，嘿，去 C++ 世界帮我获取这个变量。

sentences.en: And it does it all, like, very transparently.
sentences.zh: 它非常透明地完成了这一切。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's pretty awesome.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太棒了。

sentences.en: So because of that strength, you can think, like, anywhere you'd want to script something.
sentences.zh: 所以因为这个优势，你可以想到，任何你想编写脚本的地方。

sentences.en: So things you might want to script, like, often you hear this in, like, video games.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能想编写脚本的事情，比如，你经常在电子游戏中听到这个。

sentences.en: So video games want to have some scripting done where you control what happens when a player swings a sword and hits somebody.
sentences.zh: 电子游戏想要进行一些脚本编写，用来控制当玩家挥剑击中某人时会发生什么。

sentences.en: You know, what, like, what happens?
sentences.zh: 你知道，会发生什么？

sentences.en: You can script that event.
sentences.zh: 你可以编写那个事件的脚本。

sentences.en: Like, I want to decrease damage by 10, and I want to, you know, trigger, affect magic lightning bolts, you know, onto the screen.
sentences.zh: 比如，我想减少 10 点伤害，我想触发魔法闪电效果在屏幕上。

sentences.en: And these kinds of things, you can imagine, like, through playtesting and stuff, you might want to tweak those.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，通过游戏测试之类的，你可能想要调整这些数值。

sentences.en: But you don't want to have to go in and actually, like, you know, edit the code or have to even know what the code means.
sentences.zh: 但你不想进去实际编辑代码，或者甚至不需要知道代码意味着什么。

sentences.en: You might want to have other people be able to make those changes.
sentences.zh: 你可能希望其他人也能进行这些更改。

sentences.en: And so scripting languages provide that flexibility to you.
sentences.zh: 所以脚本语言为你提供了这种灵活性。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, most of these game studios, the people who are creating the content, they're not programmers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大多数游戏工作室，那些创造内容的人，他们不是程序员。

sentences.en: You know, they're just, they're often, like, game designers who are just sort of, like, playing with the different variables.
sentences.zh: 他们通常是游戏设计师，只是在摆弄不同的变量。

sentences.en: Like, oh, if I make magic more powerful, how does that affect the game?
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，如果我让魔法更强大，会对游戏产生什么影响？

sentences.en: And let me play for a few hours on this setting.
sentences.zh: 让我用这个设置玩几个小时看看。

sentences.en: And they can't afford, even if they did know how to program, they can't afford to be recompiling code all the time and things like that.
sentences.zh: 即使他们知道如何编程，他们也负担不起一直重新编译代码之类的事情。

sentences.en: They want to just make changes quick.
sentences.zh: 他们只想快速做出更改。

sentences.en: And so Lua sort of gives them that flexibility.
sentences.zh: 所以 Lua 为他们提供了这种灵活性。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, Lua is also very faSt.
sentences.zh: 没错，Lua 也非常快。

sentences.en: You know, the, because it only has tables, basically hash tables, you know, it doesn't have to do a lot of thinking.
sentences.zh: 因为只有表，基本上就是哈希表，它不需要进行大量的思考。

sentences.en: It doesn't have a lot of complicated instructions or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 它没有很多复杂的指令之类的东西。

sentences.en: And so the execution speed is awesome.
sentences.zh: 所以执行速度非常棒。

sentences.en: And you can even use Lua on, like, embedded devices and things like that, which don't have a lot of, don't have strong processors and not worry about it.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在嵌入式设备上使用 Lua，这些设备没有强大的处理器，也不用担心。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Some good strengths and weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 一些优点和缺点。

sentences.en: I think you already alluded to the fact that they really only have tables and meta tables.
sentences.zh: 我想你已经提到了他们真的只有表和元表这一事实。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that's a strength that it's very simple that way.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，它非常简单，这是一个优点。

sentences.en: But also, like everything, that can be a weakness as well.
sentences.zh: 但就像所有事物一样，这也可以是一个缺点。

sentences.en: That it doesn't always obvious how to get what you need to get done.
sentences.zh: 因为并不总是显而易见如何完成你需要做的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: I mean, people have tried to shoehorn so much into the tables and meta tables.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们试图把太多东西硬塞进表和元表里。

sentences.en: Like, someone created, like, a class-based infrastructure where, you know, if you have getters and setters as, like, items, keys in the table.
sentences.zh: 比如，有人创建了一个基于类的基础设施，如果你有 getter 和 setter 作为表中的键。

sentences.en: But it's really hacky.
sentences.zh: 但这真的很蹩脚。

sentences.en: And then once you start doing things like that, performance sort of goes down the tubes because the language isn't really designed for that.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始做这类事情，性能就会一落千丈，因为该语言并不是为此而设计的。

sentences.en: But it's not really designed for you to hit a meta table every time you want to access a variable.
sentences.zh: 它并不是设计用来让你每次想访问变量时都去访问元表的。

sentences.en: And the other weakness is that it's just not very fully featured.
sentences.zh: 另一个缺点是它功能不够全面。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, no one's taken the time to bind your favorite library to Lua.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有人花时间把你最喜欢的库绑定到 Lua 上。

sentences.en: Chances are.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: You know, like, I mean, if you really like fluid dynamics or you want to use, like, some kind of physics engine or if you want to do something like some kind of heavy, like,
sentences.zh: 如果你真的很喜欢流体动力学，或者你想使用某种物理引擎，或者如果你想做一些繁重的微分方程之类的计算，

sentences.en: differential equations or something, you know, chances are that that hasn't been, you know, there's no binding for Lua for that.
sentences.zh: 很有可能没有 Lua 的绑定。

sentences.en: And that's mainly because, you know, Lua is designed to sort of be a supplement to another language.
sentences.zh: 这主要是因为 Lua 被设计为另一种语言的补充。

sentences.en: So, you're just not going to get the kind of features you get.
sentences.zh: 所以你不会得到你在其他语言中得到的那种功能。

sentences.en: Like in Python, for example, if you want to just, let's say you have, you're streaming out a bunch of data to disk and you want that data to be compressed.
sentences.zh: 比如在 Python 中，如果你想把一堆数据流式传输到磁盘并进行压缩。

sentences.en: Well, there's a gzip, you know, library, like, which is part of the Python standard library.
sentences.zh: 有一个 gzip 库，它是 Python 标准库的一部分。

sentences.en: So, there's compression built in.
sentences.zh: 所以内置了压缩功能。

sentences.en: You can say, look, write this to disk and make it compressed so that it doesn't take up as much space.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，把这个写到磁盘并压缩，这样它就不会占用太多空间。

sentences.en: You're not going to find that kind of functionality in Lua.
sentences.zh: 你在 Lua 中找不到这种功能。

sentences.en: So, if you need those kind of bindings, you're going to have to write them yourself, which could be really tedious.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你需要这些绑定，你必须自己写，这可能非常乏味。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But there are some libraries.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些库。

sentences.en: It's not to say that it's not fully featured or functional.
sentences.zh: 并不是说它功能不全。

sentences.en: And we have a link here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有一个链接。

sentences.en: But, I mean, there are libraries for it.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，确实有相关的库。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's fairly well supported.
sentences.zh: 而且它得到了相当好的支持。

sentences.en: It's not, again, being around so long, it kind of has to be.
sentences.zh: 它存在了这么久，不得不这样。

sentences.en: And it's just one of those things you're going to have to go in and say, this is what I get.
sentences.zh: 这只是你需要去接受的事情之一，这就是我能得到的。

sentences.en: And not expect that when you find a cool tool that it will have a binding for Lua.
sentences.zh: 不要指望当你找到一个很酷的工具时，它会有 Lua 绑定。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, to Patrick's point, there's a, we post a link, we'll post a link on the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，针对 Patrick 的观点，我们发布了一个链接，我们会在节目说明中发布一个链接。

sentences.en: And there is a ton of, there are a ton of, you know, different libraries for Lua and things like that.
sentences.zh: Lua 有大量的不同库之类的东西。

sentences.en: So, definitely, I wouldn't shy away from it because of that.
sentences.zh: 所以，绝对的，我不会因为这个而避开它。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, definitely, if you have some existing application and you find yourself just constantly recompiling it and changing constants and recompiling it,
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你有一个现有的应用程序，发现自己不断地重新编译它，更改常量，然后重新编译，

sentences.en: then you probably should just be using Lua.
sentences.zh: 那么你可能应该使用 Lua。

sentences.en: So, the people that use it, I mean, we talked about it tends to be scripting.
sentences.zh: 所以，使用它的人，我们谈到它往往用于脚本编写。

sentences.en: So, World of Warcraft uses Lua as their scripting engine.
sentences.zh: 《魔兽世界》使用 Lua 作为其脚本引擎。

sentences.en: So, you know, other people, I know there's some mods and stuff that are written with scripting language in Lua.
sentences.zh: 所以，其他人，我知道有一些模组是用 Lua 脚本语言编写的。

sentences.en: Also, I use this program to do some photo editing, Lightroom, which is an Adobe product that does workflow for taking pictures and editing them and then, you know,
sentences.zh: 此外，我使用这个程序进行一些照片编辑，Lightroom，这是 Adobe 的产品，用于拍摄照片、编辑照片的工作流程，然后，你知道，

sentences.en: kind of making libraries or catalogs and saving them out.
sentences.zh: 建立库或目录并保存它们。

sentences.en: And all the UI in there was scripted in Lua.
sentences.zh: 里面的所有 UI 都是用 Lua 编写脚本的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, UI is an obvious choice.
sentences.zh: 没错，我的意思是，UI 是一个显而易见的选择。

sentences.en: So, in general, just to talk a little bit about things like why you need scripting, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，总的来说，我们先简单聊聊为什么要用脚本语言，对吧？

sentences.en: Now, we talked about a couple of the reasons, you know, with the recompiling and things like that.
sentences.zh: 刚才我们讨论了其中的几个原因，比如重新编译之类的那些事儿。

sentences.en: But also, some things like UI specifically is just a pain to write in a, you know, statically typed language like C++.
sentences.zh: 但还有一点，特别是 UI，用 C++ 这种静态类型语言来写简直是种折磨。

sentences.en: So, for example, let's say, you know, you want to hit a button or a menu item.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，假设你想点击一个按钮或菜单项。

sentences.en: And when you hit that button, you want a function to be called.
sentences.zh: 当你点击那个按钮时，你希望调用一个函数。

sentences.en: Well, in C++, to do that, you have to create some kind of interface class.
sentences.zh: 在 C++ 中，要做到这一点，你必须创建一个接口类。

sentences.en: It's a virtual class, which has some method called, you know, like perform function.
sentences.zh: 那是一个虚类，里面有个叫执行函数之类的方法。

sentences.en: And then all of your classes, which need to have this function, need to inherit from that class.
sentences.zh: 然后所有需要这个功能的类，都必须继承自那个类。

sentences.en: And you need to, like, downcast the class when you pass it into the button.
sentences.zh: 而且当你把它传给按钮时，还得进行向下转型。

sentences.en: And it just, you have to go through all these hoops, right?
sentences.zh: 你得绕这么多弯子，对吧？

sentences.en: But if you have an interpreted language like Lua, which is driving your GUI, then you can just bind different actions to different buttons.
sentences.zh: 但如果你用像 Lua 这样的解释型语言来驱动 GUI，就可以直接把不同的动作绑定到不同的按钮上。

sentences.en: And Lua doesn't care about the types of the, you know, actions.
sentences.zh: Lua 根本不在乎那些动作的类型。

sentences.en: So, it doesn't care if, like, oh, this one function was part of a class.
sentences.zh: 它不在乎这个函数是不是某个类的一部分。

sentences.en: And now, like, you have to do all sorts of crazy wizardry to get access to that.
sentences.zh: 而在 C++ 里，你得施展各种奇技淫巧才能访问到它。

sentences.en: Lua, you know, because it's a scripting language, it doesn't have any of that overhead.
sentences.zh: Lua 因为是脚本语言，完全没有这些开销。

sentences.en: And so, it makes it great for doing UI.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常适合用来做 UI。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, Lua.
sentences.zh: 所以，Lua。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Give it a shot, man.
sentences.zh: 试试看吧，伙计。

sentences.en: Don't write your UI in C++ if you can help it.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，别用 C++ 写 UI。

sentences.en: So, on general notes, I guess meta notes, kind of like meta tables.
sentences.zh: 那么，回到一般性话题，我想是元话题，有点像元表那样。

sentences.en: Anyways, we have gotten some good feedback from people, some extra language suggestions,
sentences.zh: 总之，我们收到了一些不错的反馈，还有一些额外的语言建议，

sentences.en: some people writing in to tell us that they've found tips or tricks that we've mentioned useful.
sentences.zh: 有些人写信告诉我们，他们觉得我们提到的技巧和窍门很有用。

sentences.en: And, as always, we appreciate that, you know.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我们对此心存感激。

sentences.en: We are always glad to be out there and helping people and at least entertaining you, hopefully.
sentences.zh: 我们总是很高兴能在这里帮助大家，至少希望能给你们带来一些乐趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全同意。

sentences.en: So, if you do have something to say, you can check us out on Google+.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有什么想说的，可以去我们的 Google+ 页面看看。

sentences.en: We have a Programming Throwdown Plus page and we're pretty good about putting the new episodes linked there.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个 Programming Throwdown Plus 页面，我们会把新剧集的链接发在那里。

sentences.en: Or, you know, if you have comments, you can, of course, put them there.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你有什么评论，当然也可以发在那里。

sentences.en: Hopefully positive, but we're willing to take criticism as well.
sentences.zh: 希望是正面的评价，但我们也愿意接受批评。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全同意。

sentences.en: And you can always, if you have something you don't necessarily want there, you can always email us at programmingthrowdown at gmail.com.
sentences.zh: 如果你有什么不想公开说的话，随时可以发邮件到 programmingthrowdown@gmail.com 联系我们。

sentences.en: Yeah, one interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 对了，有一件有趣的事。

sentences.en: Somebody wrote in and said that I guess they can't access the G Plus page unless they have a G Plus account.
sentences.zh: 有人写信说，如果他们没有 G Plus 账号，好像就无法访问我们的 G Plus 页面。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 是真的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我也不清楚。

sentences.en: To be honest, I haven't tried.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我还没试过。

sentences.en: We shall try.
sentences.zh: 我们得去试试。

sentences.en: I thought it was public.
sentences.zh: 我以为那是公开的。

sentences.en: Like, I thought there was a public section.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我以为有一个公开的部分。

sentences.en: But, yeah, as Patrick was saying, just to reiterate, if you can't access us on G Plus for whatever reason, don't hesitate to shoot an email to programmingthrowdown at gmail.com.
sentences.zh: 不过，正如 Patrick 所说，再强调一遍，如果因为任何原因你无法在 G Plus 上访问我们，请随时发送电子邮件至 programmingthrowdown@gmail.com。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I guess if you can't see the Plus page, you can also check out the blog.
sentences.zh: 没错，我想如果你看不到 Plus 页面，也可以去看看我们的博客。

sentences.en: Oh, that's right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对的。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Programmingthrowdown.blogspot.com.
sentences.zh: Programmingthrowdown.blogspot.com.

sentences.en: Yeah, you can follow the blog.
sentences.zh: 你可以关注我们的博客。

sentences.en: We definitely cross-post everything on there.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对会在上面同步发布所有内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so then there's also you can put comments there.
sentences.zh: 是的，你也可以在上面发表评论。

sentences.en: And I believe that generates.
sentences.zh: 我想那应该会生成通知。

sentences.en: We don't check that very often, but I think it does actually send us an email when somebody posts a comment there.
sentences.zh: 我们不常检查那个，但我想当有人发表评论时，它确实会给我们发邮件。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we try to be easy to reach.
sentences.zh: 所以我们尽量让大家容易联系到我们。

sentences.en: We're here for you people.
sentences.zh: 我们是为你们服务的。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: You know, if you have any, you know, we've had a couple of requests, and we want to fulfill the requests.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们收到了一些请求，我们希望能满足这些请求。

sentences.en: So definitely Java is going to be coming down the pipe, and Go is going to be coming down the pipe.
sentences.zh: 所以 Java 和 Go 肯定会安排上的。

sentences.en: Oh, you're foreshadowing.
sentences.zh: 哦，你这是在剧透啊。

sentences.en: Now we have a lot to live up to.
sentences.zh: 现在我们压力很大了。

sentences.en: But if there are any other requests from the audience, don't hesitate.
sentences.zh: 但如果听众还有其他要求，请尽管提。

sentences.en: We definitely read every one of them, and, you know, we have a backlog that we're getting to.
sentences.zh: 我们一定会阅读每一条建议，而且我们有一个待处理的清单。

sentences.en: Yeah, and don't be offended if we don't reply to you or, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果我们没有回复你，或者诸如此类的情况，请不要介意。

sentences.en: We are listening.
sentences.zh: 我们都在听。

sentences.en: We are taking it in.
sentences.zh: 我们都记下了。

sentences.en: And, yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Hopefully we'll get there one day.
sentences.zh: 希望有一天我们能完成。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, if you say you want a language, you're going to get it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你说你想了解某种语言，你一定会看到的。

sentences.en: It just might, it's just in the pipeline.
sentences.zh: 只是可能需要一点时间，还在排队中。

sentences.en: I'm actually surprised.
sentences.zh: 其实我很惊讶。

sentences.en: I did make up a list, and the list is pretty long.
sentences.zh: 我确实列了个清单，而且清单很长。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of languages to go through.
sentences.zh: 所以还有很多语言要讲。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全同意。

sentences.en: And then probably it's one of those things where more, is there more created than we're talking about?
sentences.zh: 这大概就是那种情况，是不是创造出来的语言比我们谈论的还要多？

sentences.en: Like, is there at least one created every two weeks?
sentences.zh: 比如，是不是每两周至少会诞生一种新语言？

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: There could be.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 糟糕。

sentences.en: We might never finish this job, Jason.
sentences.zh: 我们可能永远也做不完这份工作了，Jason。

sentences.en: Oh, it could go on forever.
sentences.zh: 哦，这可能会没完没了。

sentences.en: Now I know how movie critics feel.
sentences.zh: 现在我体会到影评人的感受了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: On that note, that's all I got, everyone.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，这就是我今天要说的全部内容了，各位。

sentences.en: Have a good time.
sentences.zh: 祝大家过得愉快。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: See you guys later.
sentences.zh: 回头见，伙计们。
